clue.text: Hard work curtailed American voices

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter of the word for hard work goes

parts.note: a chore is a tedious, hard task

explanation.surface: Tough labour has been cut back, say American voices raised in complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is a group of singers, a body of voices heard together.

clue.text: Vocal fellow having a lot of solid passion about United

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word for solid, so its last letter goes

parts.note: hard means solid or firm

indicators.note: about means the word for passion surrounds the letter for United

parts.note: anger is a strong passion
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A loud man with plenty of firm feeling about his football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A haranguer delivers loud, forceful speeches, a man who is very vocal.

clue.text: Sailor picked up after old naval issue, producing dance

indicators.note: after means the sailor comes after the drink

parts.note: the Royal Navy formerly issued a daily rum ration

indicators.note: picked up means lifted, so in this down entry the sailor is read upwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor, merry on his navy rum ration, takes to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Prompt to secure right place for foot

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the phrase for prompt holds the letter for right

parts.note: to stir up is to provoke or prompt

explanation.surface: A rider is urged to put their foot firmly in the right spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop hanging from a saddle in which a rider rests a foot.

clue.text: Position taken by funny guy in short communication

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a card is an amusing, eccentric person

explanation.surface: A comedian has taken up a job, mentioned in a brief message.
explanation.definitionFit: A postcard carries only a few lines, a brief written message sent through the mail.

clue.text: Film such as Ben-Hur denied opening

indicators.note: denied opening means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: Ben-Hur is a famous epic film

explanation.surface: A grand movie is refused its premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is informal shorthand for a picture, a motion picture.

clue.text: International body brought in Green, aiming for illumination

indicators.note: brought in means the body's letters are placed inside the word for green

parts.note: a sward is an expanse of grass, a green
the UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: The United Nations takes on an environmental cause in a quest for enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the environmental party but means a stretch of lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunward means directed towards the sun, which is the source of light.

clue.text: Accountant allowed to show vivacity inside motor car

indicators.note: inside means the word for vivacity sits within the other two pieces

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
let means allowed
brio is liveliness or vivacity

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper is permitted to show some spirit while in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a convertible.

clue.text: Poet penning end of work in anger

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the word for anger holds the letter

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A writer finishes their work in a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was an Austrian poet, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Small drink not entirely a major concern

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is not given complete, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: to make a drama of something is to treat it as a major concern or fuss

explanation.surface: A little drink, it is suggested, is hardly something to worry about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small measure of spirits, especially whisky.

clue.text: Universities about to seize lecturer that's brought in old South American books of historic importance

indicators.note: brought in means all of this is placed inside the name of the old people

parts.note: the Inca were an ancient people of Peru

indicators.note: about means the two university letters go around the word for seize

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, so two of them give two U's
to nab is to seize or grab

explanation.surface: Universities hire a lecturer to bring in rare old Latin American books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universities' supplies two U's, one per university; the Inca of Peru are the 'old South American' people.
explanation.definitionFit: Incunabula are the earliest printed books, produced before 1501, prized by collectors and historians.

clue.text: Heading off for entertainment venue? That's not right

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed from the word for the venue

parts.note: a funfair is a travelling show of rides and stalls

explanation.surface: Someone is turned away on the way to a show and protests at the injustice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unfair is unjust, not fair or right.

clue.text: Historic leader taking a risk, having snake draped around

indicators.note: draped around means the snake's letters are wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
dice stand for chance or risk, as in dicing with death

explanation.surface: A daring chieftain gambles with a serpent hung about the shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: BOADICEA is the older spelling of Boudicca, queen of the Iceni, who led a revolt against Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Boadicea was the British tribal queen who led an uprising against the Romans, a famous leader of history.

clue.text: London suburb that's not all there?

explanation.surface: A quip about a London district being slightly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking is a district of east London, and as slang it means mad, mentally not all present.

clue.text: Bare worthless stuff accepted by a French revolutionary

indicators.note: accepted by means the worthless stuff goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: une is French for a (feminine)
pap is worthless, insipid material
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A French radical is handed rubbish, and is left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' is the feminine article une, and a 'revolutionary' is a red, a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that is unpapered has no wallpaper on it, so it is bare.

clue.text: Rope and so on in fictional ranch

indicators.note: fictional means made up, so the letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Lassoes and other gear on a made-up cattle spread.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ponderosa is the Cartwright family's ranch in the TV western Bonanza, so 'fictional' also suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ponderosa is the ranch at the centre of the American TV western Bonanza.

clue.text: No source given for film speed

indicators.note: no source means the first letter of the word for film is dropped

parts.note: a flick is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: A film's frame rate is quoted with no reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Lick is an informal word for speed, as in going at quite a lick.

clue.text: Some ammunition vehicle on top of hill

indicators.note: on top of means, in this down entry, the vehicle comes above the hill

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
a ridge is a long hilltop

explanation.surface: A wagon of shells sits at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a case holding a bullet and its charge, a unit of ammunition.

clue.text: I run over note for club

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
N is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A golfer chasing a ball reports running over a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a type of golf club with a metal head.

clue.text: Crude tear repaired, holding in liquid

indicators.note: holding means the result contains the word in

parts.note: raw means crude or unrefined

indicators.note: repaired means the letters are put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rough rip is mended so that it keeps fluid inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' gives RAWATER; 'holding' then puts the clue's own 'in' inside that, after its second letter. 'Crude' looks like crude oil, but it means raw.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainwater is the water that falls as rain, a liquid.

clue.text: Devastating one with sense to support sport

indicators.note: to support means, in this down entry, to sit under, so the other pieces come below the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union
I is the Roman numeral one
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A sensible person backing a sport does something crushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous means causing ruin, hugely destructive.

clue.text: Little test of network showing evidence of leak

parts.note: wee means small or little
a ping is a signal sent to check a network connection

explanation.surface: A small network check reveals data escaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leak' looks like a data leak but means a drip of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeping joint or pipe oozes moisture, a sign that it leaks.

clue.text: Motoring offence? Went in US prison? Not half

indicators.note: in means the word for went is placed inside the shortened prison name
not half means only one half of the prison's name is used

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State
to go is a euphemism for urinating, so went can mean peed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a driver's crime was relieving themselves in an American jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like travelling, but it means relieved oneself. The question mark admits that the definition is just one example of a motoring offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding, driving faster than the limit, is a common example of an offence on the road.

clue.text: You may go when you've paid it

definitions.text: You may go when you've paid it

parts.words: You may go when you've paid it
parts.note: go means use the toilet; the British phrase spend a ... comes from old coin-operated public lavatories

explanation.surface: A notice granting permission to leave once a fee is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' seems to mean depart; it means visit the lavatory, as public toilets in Britain once had a coin lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth one hundredth of a pound, once the fee for a public toilet in Britain.

clue.text: Rod recalled that man pocketing Queen in card game

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the rod's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cue is the rod used in snooker and billiards

indicators.note: pocketing means the word for that man takes the queen's letter inside

parts.note: he refers to that man
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A snooker player takes a queen ball while playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Euchre is a trick-taking card game popular in North America.

clue.text: Burden fit to be tied?

definitions.meaning: fit to be tied means furious, very angry; a mark tied together from two strokes

explanation.surface: Someone weighed down by trouble is close to losing their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross is a burden one must bear, and cross also means angry, furious.

clue.text: A new indication to proceed with old classic car these days

parts.note: a nod is a sign of approval to go ahead
the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A fresh go-ahead is given for driving a vintage motor in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Anno Domini, the AD of dates, places events in the Christian era, our present times.

clue.text: Uncertainties following invading island

indicators.note: invading means the letter for following enters the island's letters

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Doubts arise after a raid on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are conditions or doubts, as in ifs and buts.

clue.text: Chances borders of old districts

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Odds are given on boundaries of historic regions being redrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the likelihoods, or chances, of something happening.

clue.text: Mental connections recalled range — succeeded getting agreement about that

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

indicators.note: about means the word of agreement wraps around the reversed range

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for range is reversed

parts.note: a span is a range or extent

explanation.surface: Remembering a mountain range, and agreeing about it, sparks mental connections.
explanation.definitionFit: Synapses are the junctions between nerve cells, the connections through which the brain works.

clue.text: Leave period cut short and that's the truth

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word for period is dropped

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone's leave has been curtailed, and that, they insist, is fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken as gospel is accepted as unquestionable truth.
